reason: E1 provides direct evidence that Pt atoms are individually dispersed in Cu nanoparticles at sufficient dilution, supporting the first premise. E2 directly shows that propylene binding is weaker on Pt/Cu SAA than on Pt nanoparticles and links this to minimized carbon deposits, supporting the second and third premises. The link to slower deactivation is a logical extension of reduced coke, which is consistent with the evidence but not directly measured in the cited passages.
premises: Pt atoms can be individually dispersed in Cu nanoparticles at sufficient dilution
Isolated Pt in Cu weakens the binding of hydrocarbon intermediates compared to Pt nanoparticles
Weaker binding of intermediates reduces coke deposition
Reduced coke deposition leads to slower catalyst deactivation
